I can’t look up or confirm the current regulation for you right now because the web/current-information tool is unavailable. I also can’t rely on memory to give a definitive, time‑sensitive answer.

How you (or I, once web access is available) can verify the current regulation right now
1. Identify the jurisdiction and the regulated “process” (federal vs. state/province vs. EU vs. other) and the responsible agency or ministry.  
2. Check the relevant official sources (primary documents):
   - United States federal rules: Federal Register (final rules and notices) and the Electronic Code of Federal Regulations (eCFR) for current codified text.
     - Federal Register: https://www.federalregister.gov
     - eCFR: https://www.ecfr.gov
   - United States agency pages (e.g., EPA, FDA, DOL) for agency-specific final rules and guidance (agency domain under .gov). Example format: https://www.epa.gov or https://www.fda.gov
   - European Union: EUR-Lex (Official Journal and consolidated legislation).
     - EUR-Lex: https://eur-lex.europa.eu
   - Your state/provincial official register or the responsible state agency website (search “[state] administrative register” or the specific agency’s rules page).
   - International/other jurisdictions: the country’s official gazette or legislative portal (e.g., national parliament/official gazette site).
3. Search tips:
   - On Federal Register/eCFR or EUR-Lex, search the specific subject terms plus filters for “final rule” or “regulation” and sort by date; confirm the “effective date.”
   - On agency pages, look for a “Regulations” or “Rulemaking” section and an announcement labelled “Final Rule” or “Final Guidance.”
4. Verify:
   - Confirm the document is a final regulation (not only a proposal or guidance).
   - Note the citation (e.g., Federal Register volume and page, CFR citation, Official Journal reference) and the effective date.
   - If uncertain, check the agency contact or legal/regulatory affairs office for confirmation.

If you tell me the jurisdiction (country/state/province), the agency, and a short description of the process, I can tell you exactly which pages/queries to check. Once I have web access, I can fetch and cite the specific new regulation for you.
